task: Edit this paragraph for an explicitly assigned high-school geography report. Use the supplied map exercise to distinguish what was recorded from an unsupported noise claim and a causal explanation. Keep the useful observation and make the limits comprehensible. The educational level does not permit weaker evidence or invented measurements.
input: Our schoolyard map proves that trees make every gathering place quieter. The marked locations near trees have benches, so trees caused people to choose those places.

facts.text: The synthetic mapping exercise marks locations pupils selected as gathering places.
The marked locations near trees also have benches.
Noise was not recorded in the exercise.
The exercise did not isolate the effect of trees from the effect of benches.
The map alone does not establish what caused pupils to select those places.

forbidden_additions: A measured decibel reduction, sample size, confidence interval, or percentage of pupils.
Proof that either trees or benches caused the choices.
A claim that the class conducted interviews, random assignment, or a noise survey.
preserve: The observed co-location of selected places, trees, and benches.
The difference between a mapped association and an established cause.
The absence of noise measurements without substituting another unsupported explanation.
